plan: I will bid slightly above my private value if I believe it's profitable, but I'm in a first-price sealed-bid auction, which is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction) in terms of strategy. In a Vickrey auction, the optimal strategy is to bid your true value. Since this is the first round and I have no history, I will bid my true value to maximize my expected profit.

I will bid slightly above what I perceive to be the second-highest bid, given my value. Since my value is $15, I want to ensure I win if the second-highest bid is below $15. I will bid $14.9 to maximize profit if I win, as it's just under my value and a common strategy in second-price auctions is to bid your true value. However, since I pay the second-highest bid, bidding slightly below my value can still secure a win if others bid low, and it reduces my risk.

My value is $47. In a second-price auction, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy, as it maximizes my expected profit regardless of other bidders' strategies. This ensures I win when my value is higher than the second-highest bid and lose when it's not, always paying less than or equal to my value.
